note: the folds — every app a person interacts through. Surfaces present ground, and they COMPOSE: each surface delegates the parts it does not own to the surface that does, so no surface re-implements a seam. One Ground@1 contract, many dream-surfaces. NAMING (2026-10-01): The Fold is the whole system; the reading/research surface is 'the fold' (the holodeck repo, renamed). The former 'the-fold' repo is being absorbed by plane and will be archived; it no longer names a surface.

surfaces.name: the fold
surfaces.presents: the reading surface — ingest, grounded statements, records, ask
surfaces.renders: Ground@1 via the fold's facing pages

surfaces.name: the-holograph
surfaces.presents: the ledger of a single run — SOURCES / RESPONSE / NOTES

surfaces.name: the-chat
surfaces.presents: the conversation — the person's words and the system's
surfaces.renders: the mouth's draw, folded with its scars and verdict

surfaces.name: the-tui
surfaces.presents: the terminal — the hand at the loom
surfaces.renders: the same Ground@1 the web surfaces render, at the shell

surfaces.name: the-council
surfaces.presents: the many claimants — comps contending, one mode surviving

composition-rule: a request enters ONE surface; every part it does not own is delegated to the surface that does, by address — never re-implemented. The surfaces share one Ground@1 schema and call each other; the redundancy is measured (swatch), never assumed.
falsifyingControl: a surface that re-implements a seam another surface already owns (a chat that re-renders the fold's ground instead of delegating), or a surface whose presented ground has no Ground@1 address, contradicts this.
